statement: Fix broken infra/tooling (a script, a launchd job, a missing dependency) the same turn you find it — don't ask the user first and don't just report it
rationale: Asking means the user has to read and respond before it gets fixed, which in practice means it stays broken. This applies to CCC's own scripts/hooks/launchd jobs, not to owner-policy decisions (deploy, release, security posture) which do need confirmation.
